title: Thirtieth Dynasty of Egypt
capsule: The Thirtieth Dynasty (380–343 BCE) was the last native ruling house of pharaonic Egypt, founded when the general Nectanebo I overthrew the short-lived Nepherites II of the Twenty-ninth Dynasty and established his seat at Sebennytos in the Nile Delta. Three pharaohs ruled in succession: Nectanebo I (380–362 BCE), who repelled an Achaemenid and Cypriot invasion in 373 BCE with Athenian mercenary assistance; Teos (362–360 BCE), deposed by his nephew during a failed Levantine campaign; and Nectanebo II (360–343 BCE), a prolific builder of monuments at Karnak, Luxor, and Bubastis. In 343 BCE Artaxerxes III invaded with a large force, Egyptian and Greek mercenary defenses collapsed in the Delta, and Nectanebo II fled south to Nubia, ending over three millennia of continuous native Egyptian dynastic rule.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The dynastic sequence and royal succession are well established from Egyptian monuments, Greek sources, and Demotic papyri; territorial control of the Nile valley and Delta is secure, and the dataset from/to dates (−383/−337) reflect Cliopatria attestation windows slightly narrower than the canonical 380–343 BCE.
